Document the details of each test case that includes the steps to be performed, pre-requisites (entry criteria), and the post-conditions (exit criteria) necessary to indicate a successful completion.

When performing this task, consider the following:

  • When a scenario is tested, what would the result look like? This is the expected result of the test case.
  • Are there any dependencies related to this case? Can the implementation of this test case run independently or are external inputs needed?
  • Are there any prerequisite conditions for a test case?
  • What needs to be verified (e.g. does the application login function as expected)?
  • What data is needed to perform the execution conditions?
  • What actions need to be performed in each step (e.g. is login to an application required)?
  • How should the action be performed (e.g. should the login window open followed by entering a username and password)?
  • What is the result of the action performed (e.g. is the login successful)?
  • Each step of the test case should consider the positive, negative, boundary and invalid values of the expected results to confirm a conclusive test.
To provide standard, repeatable testing that validates that the solution requirements are fulfilled.
